english:
I am the one who remains, 
= I am the one who remains with them,
= born of ignorance, ignorance-born 
darkness.
*
Shrimad Bhagavad Gita, 
illuminated by the lamp of knowledge.
=
=
I give them the light of knowledge, 
= which dispels the darkness of ignorance.
= This is the explanation: 'I remove the ignorance-born darkness from them' - from those 
darkness' - from the hearts of those devotees, 
there is no worldly desire at all. 
Not even the desire for liberation (from the cycle of birth and death) is present in them. 
The implication is that they do not desire worldly things and nor do they desire 
liberation (from the cycle of birth and death). 
They only engage in my worship with love and devotion. 
When I see their selfless nature and their loving devotion to me, 
my heart is filled with joy. 
I want to serve them, to be of some use to them, 
but they do not take anything from me. 
Therefore, due to my heart being filled with joy, 
I am overcome with compassion and remove the ignorance-born darkness from them. 
The reason for my heart being filled with joy is that there is no deficiency of any kind in my devotees.

4
'Atma-bhava-stha' - A person considers himself to be 'I am' 
in the sense of 'I am this body' 
and this 'I am' is generally associated with the body. 
That is, they consider themselves to be the same as their body 
and consider their body to be changing, 
just as 'I am a child', 'I am a youth', 'I am strong', 'I am weak', etc. 
However, if we look at the essence of things, 
the 'I am' that is inherent in all living beings is independent of nature. 
This 'I am' is the one that remains forever. 
This is the meaning of the word 'Atma-bhava-stha'.

*
I remove the ignorance-born darkness with the light of knowledge. 
The implication is that I remove the ignorance that is the cause of the question, 
'Who am I?' and 'What is my nature?' 
That is, I give them the knowledge of their true nature. 
The scriptures describe the glory of this knowledge, 
and it is not necessary for them to perform any sadhanas (spiritual practices), 
nor do they need to make any effort. 
Rather, I myself give them this knowledge. 

A special point to note is that when devotees are completely devoted to me, 
I give them both detachment from the world and knowledge of their true nature. 
This is because when a devotee is completely devoted to me, 
I take care of their worldly needs (yogakshema) (Gita, Chapter 9, Verse 22). 
Similarly, I give detachment from the world and knowledge of their true nature 
to those who are completely devoted to me. 
Even after giving them these things, I remain indebted to them. 
In the Bhagavatam, the Lord says that the gopis' debt to him is so great 
that even if they were to live for a long time, 
they would not be able to repay it. 
This is because even great sages and ascetics are unable to break free from 
the bonds of attachment to their own bodies, 
but the gopis were able to break free from these bonds.

Devotees are so absorbed in my worship that 
1-(1) 
They do not accept even the highest kind of liberation (moksha) 
without my love and devotion. 
(2) 
They do not consider even the highest kind of liberation (moksha) 
to be worthy of their attention, 
and they are attracted to my love and devotion. 
(3) 
I do not deliver even the most noble and virtuous devotees 
from their own karma, 
even if they live for a long time. 
(4) 
Even if they are able to deliver them from their karma, 
they would not be able to repay the debt they owe to me. 
(5) 
This is because even the most powerful and wise beings are unable to break free 
from the bonds of attachment to their own bodies, 
but I am able to break free from these bonds.

मुक्तियोंको देनेपर भी नहीं लेते।'
(Shrimad Bhagavatam, Chapter 3, Verse 29, Verse 13)

(Shrimad Bhagavatam, Chapter 10, Verse 32, Verse 22)
